subject: MAP checkpoint — data handling & deployment decision log
thread_summary: Weekly MAP checkpoint focusing on deployment mode choices (VPC vs on-prem), retention windows, and PII handling. Agreed milestones, owners, and a follow-up meeting scheduled. Technical clarifications required for on-prem installer, KMS, and network diagrams.

From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@clearsight.com>

Cc: Pamela Ortiz <pamela.ortiz@clearsight.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff — data handling & deployment decisions

Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our current MAP workbook (ClearSight_MAP_v3.xlsx) — section 2 covers data handling requirements and preferred deployment modes. High-level asks from our security and compliance teams:

- We need clarity on options for VPC/private deployment (network topology, peering requirements).
- On-prem installer availability and supported OS/hardware matrix.
- Retention controls: ability to configure token-level and KV/cache retention windows, and a minimum retention guarantee for audit logs.
- PII handling: redaction/transform at ingress and enforceable encryption at rest with customer-managed keys.

Can you confirm who from your side will own technical follow-ups and propose a timeline for the MAP milestones (eval -> pilot -> production)? We are working toward a decision by end of May.

Attaching MAP workbook for reference.

Thanks,
Jared
Jared Cole
Head of Security Programs
ClearSight Health

Thanks Jared — appreciate the clear asks and the MAP file. I’ve looped in Marcus (platform eng) to own the technical follow-ups and Laura (cc via separate note) to own the MAP timeline and commercial milestones. Next steps:

1) Marcus to confirm VPC/network and on-prem installer details (due Wed 5/6).
2) Security Q&A: we’ll provide a short SOC2 FAQ + KMS options (customer-managed KMS supported in Private/On-prem and Dedicated via BYOK in our dedicated offering).
3) Laura to propose MAP milestones and a draft mutual action plan with dates (due Fri 5/8).
4) Schedule a 30-min checkpoint next week to align owners and finalize decision gates.

For the record: Redwood supports three serving modes — Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU in a cloud VPC), and Private (VPC or on-prem installer). On PII: we provide configurable ingress filters and token-level KV cache TTLs; persistent storage is encrypted and can be backed by customer KMS in Private deployments. I’ll let Marcus add specifics.

Proposed checkpoint: Tue 5/12 11:00 PT. Does that work for your team?

Best,
Sofia Ivanova

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff — data handling & deployment decisions

Jared / Sofia — quick technical summary to address the items in the MAP workbook. I’ll own the technical checklist and delivery of artifacts (network diagram, installer checklist, KMS integration notes). Key points: 

- VPC/Dedicated: We support VPC peering and private link. Required inbound rules are minimal (for control plane telemetry we use outbound-only TLS to our control endpoints; data plane can be entirely in customer VPC for Private deployments). I will attach a sample network diagram in our next message.
- On-prem installer: we provide an appliance-like installer (docker-compose + systemd service) for x86_64 Linux (RHEL/CentOS 8+, Ubuntu 20.04+). Minimum: 4 GPUs (NVIDIA A100/RTX6000 equivalent), 64GB RAM for a small pilot. We do not currently support ARM on-prem.
- Retention controls: Per-route TTLs for KV cache and configurable persistent storage retention windows (30 / 90 / 365 days); audit logs can be exported to your SIEM and retained per your policy — we can also set a write-once archive (WORM) to object storage for compliance.
- PII: We support ingress redaction rules and an evaluation-mode transform pipeline for tokenization/PHI detection. For full HIPAA workflows, customers should pair Private deployment with customer-managed KMS (HSM integration available via partner) and enable encrypted logs + limited admin RBAC.

Action items I’ll deliver by Fri 5/8: 
- Network diagram (PDF)
- On-prem installer checklist and supported OS/hardware matrix (PDF)
- KMS integration note and sample Terra/Cloud resource policy (txt)

Questions for ClearSight: Do you require FIPS-certified KMS? Any specific minimum retention beyond 365 days? Also, please confirm whether the pilot will run in your cloud VPC or strictly on-prem.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: MAP kickoff — data handling & deployment decisions

Marcus — thanks for the summary. A couple clarifications from our compliance team: 

- This is a HIPAA scope evaluation. FIPS KMS is not strictly required but we do need HSM-backed customer KMS for production.
- Retention: audit logs must be retained for a minimum of 7 years for certain data classes (we provided the classification in the MAP worksheet). Can Redwood support a 7-year archival path for logs and redacted records?
- On-prem pilot: we prefer an initial on-prem pilot (air-gapped rack) to validate latency and network isolation. We will share provisioning details after confirming supported OS and hardware.

I’m attaching a short compliance FAQ we keep internally to help you map controls (SOC2-FAQs.pdf). Please confirm whether your installer supports offline install (no outbound to control plane) for a fully air-gapped pilot; if not, we’ll need a phone call to discuss compensating controls.

Best,
Pamela Ortiz
Director, Information Security
ClearSight Health
